title: Counterexamples to graph compactness and two-degenerate extremal bounds
abstract: Formalizes two counterexamples in extremal graph theory. The first gives a finite family of connected bipartite cyclic graphs whose family extremal number grows strictly slower than every member's extremal number, disproving the Erdős--Simonovits compactness conjecture. The second constructs a connected bipartite two-degenerate graph with extremal number at least c n^(3/2+ε), disproving the proposed universal n^(3/2) upper bound under the stated bipartition degree condition.

informal.CompactnessConjecture.quantitativeCompac: There is a nonempty finite family of connected bipartite cyclic graphs such that every member has a uniform positive n^(4/3)-scale extremal lower bound, while every family-free host on n vertices has its sixteenth power of the edge count bounded by a constant times n^21. Consequently the family is not compact and the Erdős--Simonovits compactness conjecture is false.
informal.TwoDegenerateGraphs.twoDegenerateExtrema: There is a connected bipartite two-degenerate finite graph H such that each side of every two-coloring has a vertex of degree greater than two, yet ex(n,H) is eventually at least c n^(3/2+ε) for some positive constants c and ε.
